paper_title: Pi in the Sky: Neutron Stars with Exceptionally Light QCD Axions
notes: Paper derives astrophysical constraints on the 'exceptionally light QCD axion' parameter space (f_a-m_a plane, expressed via epsilon = (m_a/m_a^QCD)^2). Main result: excludes 5e-7 <~ epsilon <~ 0.2 for m_a >~ 2e-9 eV from neutron-star thermal relaxation, isolated NS cooling, and pulsar glitches. Tables IV/V/VII give min/max excluded epsilon for m_a >~ 1e-8 eV (conservative Scenario A: cooling 5.2e-7-0.068, thermal relaxation 2.2e-3-0.10, glitches 8.3e-3-0.17). The excluded region is a HORIZONTAL band in epsilon, essentially mass-independent for m_a >~ 1e-8 eV. Emitted data points represent the lower (5e-7) and upper (0.2) edges of the excluded epsilon band spanning the stated mass validity range; these are NOT f_a values. Converting epsilon to f_a requires m_a-dependent QCD relation and was not done here to avoid corrupting values. Astrophysical bound, no local DM density. This is the AxionMass/f_a-m_a plane but the natural variable is epsilon; downstream conversion may be needed.
